chief_complaint: Advanced chronic kidney disease (stage 4) with evaluation for kidney transplantation, complicated by ischemic heart disease, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, anemia and recent urinary tract infection.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is an 84‑year‑old man with a long history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity and metabolic syndrome that have progressed to diabetic nephropathy. CKD advanced from stage 1 in 1990 to stage 4 in 2018 and he is currently awaiting kidney transplantation. He has ischemic heart disease with prior coronary artery bypass grafting (1981) and requires nitroglycerin and beta‑blocker therapy for angina. Diabetes is treated with basal‑bolus insulin and metformin (though metformin may be unsafe given his renal function). He has chronic anemia treated with epoetin (not captured in the medication list). In August 2020 he had an acute infective cystitis. He also reports chronic low‑back pain, gingivitis, and unhealthy alcohol use since early 2021. Vital signs are within normal limits (BP 108/79 mmHg, HR 71 bpm). Laboratory data are incomplete; the recorded HbA1c of 2.3 % is likely erroneous.
